notes : * both numeric and other common pain intensity scales/tools may be used at this point. 14 the selection methodology for these artistic stimuli was based on principles of inclusivity and representational diversity, with the objective of facilitating meaningful emotional resonance across a wide patient demographic. although an optimal protocol would incorporate direct patient engagement and multi-stakeholder input in the selection process, this was beyond the scope of the present study and remains a priority for future iterations. selection criteria encompassed a range of artistic styles (e.g, expressionism, surrealism, abstract expressionism) and time periods, including both figurative and non-figurative works, to accommodate diverse aesthetic preferences and cultural sensitivities. artwork selection was conducted collaboratively by the study authors, comprising specialists in pain medicine, psychiatry, qualitative and quantitative research methodology, and oral and maxillofacial surgery, drawing on their interdisciplinary clinical and academic perspectives. the process was aligned with the study's aim of facilitating reflective engagement with pain. an initial pool of artworks was compiled by the research team, from which selections were made through iterative review and consensus based on the predefined criteria. recruitment and sampling the qualitative component of this study was embedded within an ongoing randomized controlled trial (rct) designed to evaluate the efficacy of the ape tool. the study was conducted at king abdulaziz university dental hospital, jeddah, saudi arabia between february and may 2025. the qualitative study was preplanned as part of the trial design. participants for the qualitative analysis were purposively sampled from the intervention arm (ape tool), which was compared to conventional pain assessment in patients with tmd. participants were identified through clinic medical records, referrals from treating clinicians, and public advertisement, and were enrolled after providing written informed consent. selection was based on participants' willingness and ability to engage in in-depth discussions of their pain experiences. all selected patients were adults diagnosed with early-stage temporomandibular disorders (tmd), specifically wilkes' stage i or ii, and were undergoing conservative, non-surgical management. exclusion criteria, applied identically in this qualitative sub-study, included need for surgical intervention, diagnosed severe psychiatric illness (e.g, psychotic disorders, bipolar affective disorder), and regular use of narcotic medication. semi-structured interviews were conducted and continued until data saturation was achieved that is, the point at which no new themes or insights emerged from subsequent interviews. an initial sample size of 10-15 patients was anticipated; 15 however, saturation was reached after interviewing 18 patients. this approach facilitated a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of both shared and individual dimensions of the patients' lived pain experiences. data saturation was determined when no new themes or conceptual insights emerged from successive interviews, and redundancy in participant responses was observed. the research team reviewed the evolving coding framework throughout data collection to assess whether additional interviews generated novel concepts or substantially expanded existing themes. recruitment ceased once thematic redundancy was consistently observed. this manuscript reports only the qualitative, phenomenological validation of the ape tool; it does not report treatment efficacy, longitudinal outcomes, or inferential statistics from the parent trial, which will be reported separately upon its completion. data collection data were collected through semi-structured, one-on-one interviews. interviews were conducted by rb and lb, oral and maxillofacial surgeons who received training in qualitative methods from mr. interviews were conducted in a private consultation room at king abdulaziz university dental hospital, lasted approximately 5-8 minutes, and were conducted in arabic or english according to participant preference. the interviewer shared no prior clinical relationship with participants before recruitment. given the study's phenomenological orientation, reflexivity was maintained throughout the research process, with the researcher acknowledging their clinical background and interest in arts-based approaches to pain as potential influences on data interpretation. both rb and lb were trained to ensure consistency in approach. prior to data collection, the interviewers were familiarized with the ape framework and trained in semi-structured interviewing techniques and followed the script in tables 1-3 . artwork selection was primarily participant-driven. participants were presented with three curated artworks and asked to select the one that most resonated with them, as it would serve as the basis for the subsequent discussion. no additional guidance or interpretation was provided to avoid influencing their choice. all three artworks were presented identically to every participant as standard-sized printed reproduction, to ensure consistency of visual stimulus across interviews. the selected artwork served as a visual and emotional prompt, facilitating the expression of personal and often complex dimensions of their pain. during the interviews, three core domains were explored: 14 symbology: how patients view the origin and journey of their pain. colors, brushstroke, and environment: how pain feels and how it impacts daily life. patients were encouraged to share their experiences in their own words, fostering a comfortable and open environment for dialogue. all interviews were audio-recorded with informed consent, fully transcribed verbatim, and anonymized to ensure participant confidentiality and data privacy. no modifications were requested from patients after the interview was conducted and only one interview per patient was carried out. no field notes were taken during the interview. data analysis to analyze the data, the study followed a structured phenomenological approach called moustakas' modified stevick-colaizzi-keen method. 16 this includes: setting aside preconceptions: "bracketing" was employed to set aside prior assumptions and enable an unbiased engagement with the data. highlighting key statements: every participant's statement was treated equally, allowing us to capture the full range of insights. clustering into meaning unites and themes: significant statements were clustered into meaning units, then grouped into overarching themes. developing textural and structural descriptions (describing what and how they experience): for each theme, a textural description (what participants experienced) was developed as well as a structural description (how the experience occurred), integrated into a composite description of the phenomenon. each transcript was read repeatedly to achieve immersion in the data. significant statements relevant to participants' lived experiences of pain were identified through horizontalization and treated with equal value. these statements were then clustered into meaning units representing shared aspects of the pain experience. meaning units were synthesized into textural descriptions capturing what participants experienced and structural descriptions describing how these experiences unfolded within their personal and contextual circumstances. finally, these descriptions were integrated to develop the essential thematic structure of the phenomenon. throughout the analysis, transcripts were revisited to identify divergent or negative cases that challenged the emerging interpretations. these cases were discussed among the research team and incorporated into the refinement of the thematic framework rather than being excluded. nvivo software was utilized to facilitate the organization and management of qualitative data, enabling systematic identification of emerging themes. finally, the findings were synthesized into a cohesive narrative describing the pain experience, capturing patients' experiences using the ape tool. coding was conducted by a single researcher (mr) with expertise in qualitative analysis, with themes reviewed and discussed with the broader research team to enhance analytical rigor. throughout the analysis, transcripts were revisited to identify divergent or negative cases that challenged the emerging interpretations. these cases were considered during refinement of the thematic framework and discussed with the broader research team to ensure that the final themes adequately reflected variation in participants' experiences. in addition, peer debriefing was conducted with two independent qualitative researchers who reviewed preliminary codes and thematic interpretations to enhance analytic rigor and reduce interpretive bias. this approach enabled the development of a rich and authentic account of patients' pain experiences and provided insight into how the ape tool supported their ability to articulate and make sense of their pain. themes were derived inductively from the data, allowing patterns and meanings to emerge directly from patients' narratives rather than being imposed a priori. the three interview domains (symbology; colors, brushstroke, and environment; emotions) structured only the sequence of interview prompts; themes reported in the results were derived inductively from participants' narrative responses rather than mapped directly onto these domains. ethical considerations this study complied with the declaration of helsinki and received approval from the institutional review board of king abdulaziz university (irb no.: 02-01-25). informed consent was obtained from all patients prior to enrollment. to address potential emotional distress during the ape interviews, a clinical psychologist was available on call, with established referral pathways in place for further psychological support if needed. confidentiality was maintained through data anonymization and secure, encrypted storage. all study instruments were translated and culturally validated for arabic-speaking patients. a multidisciplinary expert committee reviewed all versions for semantic, idiomatic, experiential, and conceptual equivalence, resolving discrepancies through documented consensus. the translated materials were piloted with 10-20 participants prior to the main study. all patients received equal clinical care, and participation in the study did not influence or alter their standard treatment trajectory. results this study explored the lived experiences of patients with tmd using the artwork pain exploration (ape) tool. during the interviews, participants used visual elements of their selected artwork as prompts to describe sensory, emotional, functional, and psychological dimensions of their pain. through phenomenological analysis of 18 interviews, five central themes emerged that characterized these experiences. of the 18 participants, 12 (66.7%) were male and 6 (33.3%) were female. age distribution was as follows: 18-24 years, n=12 (66.7%); 25-34 years, n=5 (27.8%); 35-44 years, n=1 (5.6%). wilkes staging was distributed as 13 (72.2%) stage i and 5 (27.8%) stage ii. theme 1: pain as a daily ritual many patients described pain as a predictable part of their daily routine, especially upon waking. they described the pain as consistent but not always intense and shaped the start of their day. patient 1: the pain is there only when i wake up. i have to open my mouth carefully because of the mouthpiece. patient 5: when i wake up in the morning, i feel pain. but during the day it starts to go away. patient 7: i wake up clenching my teeth, and that's when i feel the pressure most. patient 6: i find myself in pain when i wake up, especially during exam periods. theme 2: adaptation and coping most patients depended on adjusting their behavior to cope with the symptoms rather than seeking medical intervention. for example, they altered their eating habits, avoided wide jaw movements, and used night guards. patient 4: i started eating slower and smaller portions. the clicking is still there, but it's not painful anymore. patient 7: i changed the habit from being a bruxer to clenching. patient 6: i just try not to talk too much or open my mouth widely. theme 3: limited emotional impact of pain despite experiencing chronic pain or discomfort, several patients reported minimal emotional distress. the pain was often described as annoying or inconvenient but did not significantly affect their mood or mental health. many patients knew how to separate themselves emotionally from the pain experience. i just don't feel like talking, but i'm not angry or sad. i can say something is bothering me, but i wouldn't call it pain. theme 4: triggered by stress or emotional states some pain was strongly associated with stress or emotional strain, that is specially during academic or personal challenges. the patients described a connection between psychological tension and the onset or worsening of the symptoms, suggesting an emotional component in their pain experiences. stress did not always originate from current life events. some patients traced it to past unresolved issues. this theme emphasizes the importance of recognizing emotional stress as a contributing factor to physical pain. patient 3: it started in university when i was very stressed. patient 6: maybe there was stress in my life. patient 8: during stressful periods, especially with family, the pain becomes worse. theme 5: disruption of social and functional activities a number of patients mentioned disruptions in their daily activities and social interactions specially when pain was intense. for example, patients discussed avoiding certain food that limit their interaction and skipping social events to prevent aggravating their pain. although some patients adapted to this, the fear of triggering the pain and discomfort affected their choices. patient 6: if i open my mouth too much, the pain will last for an hour. patient 4: sometimes i can't eat what i want. it's annoying when i'm out with people and can't enjoy the food. patient 8: i avoid talking in social gatherings. the findings suggest that the ape-guided interviews provided participants with an opportunity to describe sensory, emotional, and functional aspects of their tmd experiences. the artworks appeared to serve as visual prompts that facilitated reflection and discussion during the interviews. discussion pain evaluation remains one of the most complex arms in the management of chronic pain patients. as it has been mentioned and emphasized by regina fink in 2000 17 that pain assessment is the cornerstone to optimal pain management as many essential/crucial treatment decisions depend on accurate pain assessment. however, pain remains inherently subjective, making standardized evaluation a persistent challenge. the subjective-objective dichotomy in pain evaluation several pain assessment methods aim to transform pain from its subjective nature to a more objective, quantifiable state. while such methods, including physiological measurements of nociception, can capture aspects of the pain response, they often fail to reflect the full pain experience. pain perception is influenced by a wide array of biopsychosocial factors, including emotional, psychological, and social components, as well as the consequences of pain such as functional limitations. from another side, the emotional and psychological components of the pain contribute to the pain experience and are also greatly affected by the pain itself. in addition, chronic pain can be underreported or overreported for several reasons. 18 the visual analogue scale is also affected by the secondary motivations. this additional information is usually gained by questionnaires as brief pain inventory. the accuracy of the pain evaluation methods varies from one to another where each one has its advantage for certain pain aspects. though tools measuring physiological responses to nociception attempt to provide objectivity, the pain includes the perception of the nociception giving the pain experience. the distinction between nociception and the lived experience of pain remains critical. for instance, the severity and perception of pain are often shaped/influenced by psychosocial factors, such as environmental stressors and coping mechanisms as well as the consequences of the pain (ex: limitation) that can also negatively superimpose the pain experience. in addition, and as described by merleau ponty in 1945, 20 the perception cannot be isolated as it is embedded in the context which determine the meaning which in consequence determines how the stimulus will be perceived. these variables may not be captured by conventional scales or physiological measurements and needs detailed description and expression. visual art as a tool for expressive pain communication recent approaches have explored the integration of visual art into the clinical setting as a way to deepen understanding of the patient's pain experience. engaging a visual art while evaluating pain is thought to offer an expressive channel for communicating and understanding not just the nature of pain but also each patient's unique experience. 14 increasing the accuracy of pain evaluation by better pain expression can lead to proper and more detailed understanding of the patients' experience and condition by a health care professional which facilitates choosing more adapted treatment options and indirectly lead to better therapeutic results. 17 in this study, we investigate whether analyzing art during pain evaluation enhances communication, provides additional diagnostic insights, allows more detailed pain expressions or description, or indirectly improves treatment outcomes through better evaluation? key findings pain patterns and dynamics the study found that pain in tmj disorder patients tends to be predictable and time-dependent, with a dynamic that is characterized by increased intensity during specific parts of the day-often higher in the morning-and a gradual fading as the day progresses. pain usually grabs the individuals' attention, as a protective mechanism from danger. this physiological protective role is known to be lost in the chronic pain condition leaving only the negative consequences, by that, affecting tasks that need attention. 21 on the other hand, this predictability of pain in chronic tmj disorder has an advantage to adapt the treatment accordingly, starting from avoiding the triggering factors to having the medication prior to the expected episodes or the usual time of the pain maximal intensity. moreover, the fading pattern of the pain allows as well better timing of medications and organizing tasks that needs attention late during the day during the time of expected faded pain. non-pharmacological management strategies many patients reported using non-pharmacological, non-interventional strategies to control their pain. these included the use of night guards, adapted mouth opening, and the modification of the eating behaviors. such strategies were reported to be effective, with some patients experiencing complete resolution of pain symptoms through consistent behavioral adaptation. this information is important for many things, one of them is the avoidance of escalating the treatment in case of satisfaction with the night guard. patients' engagement in the management of their pain is important, and it is illustrated somehow in the previous example by the adaptive reactions to their pathology with great efficacy. while standard tools like the beck depression inventory (bdi) and the profile of mood states (poms) questionnaires are typically used to assess the emotional burden of chronic pain, patients in this study have mentioned that aspect clearly. psychosocial triggers and stress factors although the pain did not significantly affect patients' overall quality of life (qol), patients frequently identified professional and social stressors as key pain triggers. this type of information is usually easily extracted by direct questions to the patients. behavioral modification and anticipatory avoidance patients demonstrated clear insight into the functional limitations imposed by their pain. many reported altering their daily habits to prevent or minimize pain episodes. this included the development of anticipatory avoidance behaviors, where patients refrained from certain activities preemptively to avoid triggering pain. while adaptive, this behavior also contributed to functional limitations, disturbance of social role leading to more stressed mindset which is a known finding in chronic pain patient-an experience consistent with broader findings in chronic pain literature. 22 interestingly, these observations were spontaneously expressed by patients, rather than being reflected by or through formal questionnaires as it is used to be done. this highlights the potential of more conversational, expressive, and personalized evaluation techniques, such as art-based assessment, to reveal deeper insights into the lived experience of chronic pain. feasibility and acceptability of the ape tool in clinical settings the tool was well-tolerated, emotionally safe, and appreciated by patients; no significant emotional distress was reported or distraction that might affect the accuracy of the evaluation. these preliminary findings suggest that arts-based interventions may be integrated without disrupting standard care, though confirmation in a larger, comparative sample is needed. the structured interview domains (symbology, color/texture, emotional impact) provide clinicians with a semi-systematic way to explore pain meaningfully. limitations and future directions this study was conducted within a single site with a purposive sample of early-stage tmd patients under conservative management, so the findings may have limited transferability to other settings or patient populations. furthermore, participants were purposively selected from the intervention arm based on their willingness and ability to engage in in-depth interviews. as a result, the findings may primarily reflect the experiences of individuals who were more comfortable expressing their thoughts and emotions, potentially limiting the transferability of the findings to less verbally expressive patients. the selection of artworks, though diverse, was not co-designed with patients. future iterations should include participatory curation. future research should explore comparative outcomes across patient populations and clinical stages, and investigate whether ape responses predict treatment adherence, psychological resilience, or clinical therapeutic outcomes through comparison with a control group or another assessment tool. although the ape tool was used to guide all interviews, the themes identified in this study primarily reflect participants' lived experiences of tmd pain rather than specific responses to individual artworks. as this exploratory qualitative study was not designed to compare the ape approach with a conventional semi-structured interview, no conclusions can be drawn regarding whether the artworks elicited qualitatively different or richer information. future comparative studies are needed to determine the distinctive contribution of the ape approach to qualitative pain assessment. conclusion this study is exploratory and it suggests that involving the visual analysis during pain interrogation can serve as a symbolic and emotional prompt, allowing patients to more freely and thoroughly express their pain experience. such expressions may reveal psychosocial dimensions and behavioral adaptations that can be missed during routine conventional pain assessment. compared to standard numeric or verbal scales, the tool adds emotional depth and personal nuance. this qualitative sub-study did not include a direct comparison against a standard, non-art interview. pain was quantitatively measured as part of the parent randomized controlled trial and will be reported separately; this manuscript reports only the qualitative, phenomenological findings from the ape interviews. by enhancing the accuracy and depth of pain evaluation, particularly in conditions like tmj disorder, clinicians may be better positioned to tailor treatment strategies, address individual pain drivers, and ultimately improve therapeutic outcomes. further research is warranted to explore how structured art analysis might be integrated into routine clinical practice. later on, a quantitative comparison between the group of the art engaged evaluation vs a controlled group (evaluation without art) can be used to check whether the addition of the art over or underestimate the pain. ethics approval this study was performed in line with the principles of reflects the extent to which taxa or communities can tolerate environmental variations, indicating their potential to respond to environmental changes. however, it remains unclear whether micro- and macro-organisms share similar patterns of niche breadth along the same environmental gradients, and which environmental filters regulates niche breadth across different trophic levels. in this study, 180 soil samples were collected from the northeastern and central qinghai-tibet plateau. by integrating microbiome sequencing with plant community surveys, we quantified niche breadth for bacteria, fungi, and plants within a multidimensional environmental space defined by principal component analysis of environmental variables. we then compared niche breadth among the three groups and identified their primary environmental drivers. the results showed that fungal communities exhibited the broadest niche breadth overall, whereas plant communities displayed the greatest variability in mean niche breadth amongst sites. elevation was a shared determinant of niche breadth in all groups, although with contrasting response patterns. bacterial and fungal communities exhibited broader niche breadths at higher elevations, whereas plant communities reached their maximum niche breadths at mid-elevations, suggesting contrasting adaptive strategies. a combination of abiotic (geography and environment) and biotic (community diversity and composition) factors better explained the variation in niche breadth. in particular, compared with the niche breadth of fungal communities, that of bacterial and plant communities was more strongly regulated by biotic factors such as community composition. we further confirmed that abiotic factors influenced the niche breadth of the three biological groups, both directly and indirectly, by shaping their biotic attributes. from the perspective of niche breadth, this study revealed distinct environmental adaptation patterns and the underlying mechanisms of different biological groups in alpine grassland ecosystems. better understanding of niche breadth patterns amongst different kingdoms of life may provide improved prediction of turnover and resilience of soil ecosystems under environmental change. species with broader niche breadths tend to persist across diverse environmental settings, while those with narrower niches are typically more specialized and potentially more sensitive to environmental change . at the community level, niche breadth reflects the aggregate ecological strategies of coexisting taxa and can inform assessments of resource-use complementarity, ecosystem stability, and resilience to disturbance . in terrestrial ecosystems, plants and soil microorganisms, including bacteria and fungi, interact closely to regulate key ecological processes such as organic matter decomposition, plant-soil feedback, and biogeochemical cycling . plants modify the availability and spatial heterogeneity of soil resources through root exudates, litter inputs, and nutrient uptake, whereas soil microorganisms influence plant growth and environmental adaptation through decomposition, nutrient cycling, and symbiotic or antagonistic interactions . because these groups coexist under the same broad gradients in climate and soil conditions, their niche breadth can be evaluated within a shared environmental framework despite differences in life history, dispersal, and resource use. however, most empirical studies have focused on niche breadth variation within single taxonomic groups or along isolated environmental gradients , leaving cross-kingdom variation in niche strategies under shared environmental conditions poorly understood. soil physicochemical properties-such as ph, organic matter content, c:n ratio, salinity, and heavy metal concentrations-are known to shape microbial niche breadth by constraining resource availability and microbial metabolic flexibility . in nutrient-poor or physiochemically stressful soils (e.g. low ph, high salinity), microbial communities often exhibit narrower niche breadths due to reduced metabolic potential and substrate access . similar effects have been observed in plant communities, where niche breadth is closely linked to soil nutrient availability, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus , which influence spatial resource partitioning and species coexistence. in addition, climatic factors-such as temperature and precipitation-act as dominant environmental filters, governing species survival, distribution, and niche expression . for instance, drought stress has been shown to constrain microbial niche breadth and promote ecological specialization , while alpine and subalpine plant communities display strong climate-dependent distributional patterns . at larger spatial scales, geographic factors, including topographic barriers, can restrict dispersal and gene flow, thereby narrowing realized niches . furthermore, macroecological studies have suggested a latitudinal gradient in niche breadth, with lower-latitude communities often characterized by narrower niches due to stable but competitive environments . while abiotic filters are key drivers of niche breadth, biotic factors-such as species diversity, community composition, and interspecific interactions-also play fundamental roles . high community diversity can promote resource partitioning and ecological specialization, thereby reducing niche overlap and overall niche breadth . interspecific relationships, including mutualism, competition, and antagonism, can reshape resource-use strategies, alter spatial structure, and influence the breadth of niches occupied . for example, bacterial succession during colonization can result in dominant taxa expanding their niche breadth under increasing competitive pressure . similarly, in tropical plant communities, rising species richness and temperature have been linked to intensified competition and reduced niche breadth . importantly, biotic effects are often context-dependent and interact with abiotic constraints . geographical isolation may intensify local environmental filtering, promote niche differentiation, or enhance niche overlap among microbial taxa . moreover, climate-driven increases in temperature or moisture can enhance diversity and interspecific competition, potentially narrowing niche breadth , while long-term climatic stability may foster ecological specialization through persistent community assembly processes . however, in terrestrial ecosystems, the formation of niche breadth is not solely determined by within-community processes, and interactions across different biological kingdoms may also play a key role . in particular, within plant-soil microbial systems, plant communities can modify the availability and spatial heterogeneity of soil resources through root exudation, litter inputs, and nutrient uptake, thereby influencing the resource-use range of bacteria and fungi . conversely, soil bacteria and fungi can regulate plant resource acquisition and environmental adaptation by mediating organic matter decomposition, nutrient cycling, pathogen suppression, and symbiotic interactions . taken together, these insights underscore the need for an integrative framework that accounts for both abiotic and biotic drivers of niche breadth. despite growing interest in understanding niche-based processes, comparative investigations across distinct biological kingdoms-particularly under shared environmental contexts-remain limited. a unified perspective that bridges microbial and plant ecology is essential for uncovering general principles of niche differentiation and for predicting how complex communities respond to global environmental change. the qinghai-tibet plateau, the world's largest alpine ecosystem, provides a natural laboratory for investigating ecological adaptation and its drivers due to its broad environmental gradients . in this study, we analysed 180 soil samples collected from the northeastern and central tibetan plateau regions and assessed niche breadths of bacteria, fungi, and plants using plant community surveys and amplicon sequencing of bacterial 16s rrna genes and fungal internal transcribed spacer (its) regions. the dataset we analysed is particularly suitable for comparison of niches because it includes a large number of standard samples where vegetation species composition, bacterial soil community, and fungal soil community were sampled together along very broad environmental gradients. here, we propose the following hypotheses: (i) due to fundamental differences in life history traits, dispersal capacity, and physiological plasticity, bacteria, fungi, and plants differ significantly in their niche breadths. (ii) despite being influenced by the same set of abiotic environmental gradients (e.g. ph, moisture, elevation), their responses along environmental gradients differ. (iii) niche breadth is determined by the interplay between abiotic constraints and biotic interactions, with the relative influence of each varying among microbial and plant communities. materials and methods sample collection a total of 60 alpine grassland sites, comprising 180 individual quadrat samples, were surveyed across the northeastern and central regions of the qinghai-tibet plateau, spanning ~815 km north-south and 960 km east-west ( fig. sampling was conducted during the peak growing season (july-august 2011) to capture peak plant and microbial activity. plant cover and species composition were recorded ( table s2 ). seven soil cores (5 cm diameter) were randomly collected from each plot. after removing the surface litter, the 0-5 cm topsoil was homogenized in the field to obtain a representative composite sample. soil samples were sieved through a 2 mm mesh to remove visible roots and litter and then split into two portions. map of the qinghai--tibet plateau showing elevation and the locations of 60 alpine grassland sampling sites across the northeastern and central plateau, with an inset indicating its position within china. vegetation survey and measurements of climate and soil properties all vascular plant species in each of the 180 plots were identified and counted in the field ( table s2 ). across all recorded plant species, forbs, sedges, grasses, and legumes accounted for 44.1%, 29.1%, 21.6%, and 5.0%, respectively. soil physicochemical properties were measured at the site level and averaged across plots. the soil ph was measured in a 1:5 (w/v) soil-to-water slurry using a ph meter (thermo orion-868, thermo orion co., waltham, ma, usa). soil moisture (sm) was determined gravimetrically. prior to analysis, air-dried soil samples were ground and passed through a 100-mesh sieve after removing visible plant residues and gravel. total carbon (tc) and total nitrogen (tn) were measured using an elemental analyser (2400 ii chn, perkinelmer, boston, ma, usa). for dissolved tn (dtn), ~5 g of fresh soil was extracted with 50 ml of 2 mol l -1 kcl solution by shaking for 1 h, followed by settling for ~30 min and filtration. for dissolved organic carbon (doc), ~5 g of fresh soil was extracted with 50 ml of deionized water by shaking for 1 h, followed by settling for ~30 min. the supernatant was centrifuged for 5 min at 4000 rpm and then filtered. the filtrates (20-30 ml) were transferred into 50 ml tubes and stored frozen prior to analysis. soil total phosphorus (stp) was determined by the molybdenum blue method with an ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometer (uv-2550; shimadzu, kyoto, japan). soil inorganic carbon (sic) was calculated from the carbonate content using calcimetry (eijkelkamp, giesbeek, the netherlands), and soil organic carbon (soc) was obtained by subtracting sic from tc. mean annual temperature (mat) and mean annual precipitation (map) were estimated by interpolating data from 716 meteorological stations across china between 1951 and 2010 (source: http://cdc.cma.gov.cn ), following the method described by jing et al. vegetation productivity was represented by the normalized difference vegetation index (ndvi) derived from modis (terra satellite; 250 m resolution, 16-day composites during july-august) obtained from nasa ( https://ladsweb.nascom.nasa.gov/data/search.html ). the study area exhibited broad climatic and edaphic heterogeneity across sampling sites ( table s3 ). soil ph ranged from 6.03 to 9.15, while sm varied from 0.003 to 1.537 g g -1 . nutrient-related variables also showed substantial variation, with tc ranging from 0.72 to 21.95 g kg -1 , tn from 0.02 to 1.66 g kg -1 , and c:n from 9.09 to 92.50. detailed descriptions and ranges of all environmental variables are provided in table s3 . for bacterial communities, the v4 region of the 16s rrna gene was amplified using the primers 515f/806r , following the protocol described by jing et al . for fungal communities, the its region was amplified using the primer pair its3/its4 as described by yang et al . sequencing was performed using the illumina miseq pe250 platform (illumina inc., san diego, ca, usa). the paired-end reads were merged using flash . sequence quality filtering, trimming, and chimaera removal were conducted using qiime v1.9.0 . bacterial taxonomic annotation was performed using the silva ssu release 138 database ( https://www.arb-silva.de/ ) , whereas fungal taxa were assigned using blastn against the unite v9.0 database ( http://unite.ut.ee ) . high-quality sequences were clustered into operational taxonomic units (otus) at 97% similarity using the usearch algorithm . after quality filtering, the average sequencing depth was 5148 reads per sample for bacterial 16s rrna genes and 64 313 reads per sample for fungal its sequences. to ensure comparability among samples and minimize biases caused by uneven sequencing depth, the feature tables were rarefied to the minimum sequencing depth across samples, resulting in 3502 reads per sample for bacteria ( table s4 ) and 11 460 reads per sample for fungi ( table s5 ). community diversity, composition, and niche breadth calculation the alpha diversity (shannon index) of bacterial, fungal, and plant communities was calculated using the diversity function in the r package vegan (version 4.1.3). bray-curtis dissimilarities were computed using the phyloseq and vegan packages, and nonmetric multidimensional scaling (nmds) was performed based on these distances. the first axis score (nmds1) was extracted as an indicator of community compositional differences (stress values: bacteria = 0.126, fungi = 0.165, and plants = 0.0002) and was calculated using the metamds function in vegan ( table s6 ). to quantify environmental niche breadth, we constructed a multidimensional environmental space based on 15 measured environmental variables across 180 sampling plots. principal component analysis (pca) was performed using the rda function in the vegan package, and the first 10 principal components, which explained 96.99% of the total environmental variation ( fig. s1 and table s7 ) were retained for subsequent analyses. otus occurring in fewer than three sampling sites were excluded prior to niche analyses to avoid unstable estimates caused by extremely low occurrence. niche breadth for each otu was calculated using the ecospat.nicheposnb function in the ecospat package . this presence-absence-based approach was used to characterize the average niche strategy within each community while reducing the influence of highly abundant taxa. differences among groups were assessed using one-way anova followed by bonferroni post hoc tests, and figures were generated using the ggplot2 package in r. statistical analyses a spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to examine the relationships between environmental variables and niche breadth, using the cor.test() function from the stats package in r. to further evaluate the relative importance of predictor variables, a random forest regression model was constructed using the scikit-learn library in python (version 1.1.3), and variable importance was quantified as the percentage increase in mean squared error (%incmse). statistical significance was assessed using permutation tests by randomly permuting the response variable and repeatedly refitting the random forest model to generate a null distribution, against which the observed %incmse values were compared to obtain p -values. variation partitioning analysis (vpa) was conducted using the varpart function in the vegan package in r to quantify the independent and joint explanatory powers of the three variable sets. we constructed a structural equation model (sem) to explore the direct and indirect effects of environmental, geographic, and biotic factors on niche breadth. the sem was implemented in amos software (version 23.0, ibm, usa). noncollinear abiotic variables (excluding tc, tn, and soc) were z-standardized. environmental dissimilarity among sites was calculated based on euclidean distances, whereas geographic dissimilarity was computed using haversine distances (via the geosphere package). community compositional dissimilarity (bray-curtis) was calculated separately for bacteria, fungi, and plants. the resulting pairwise distance matrices were then integrated by matching sample pairs to generate a combined cross-kingdom dissimilarity dataset. shannon diversity values for bacteria, fungi, and plants were combined and standardized, and pairwise diversity dissimilarity among samples was then calculated using manhattan distances. in sem modelling, we constructed a three-layer path structure based on theoretical assumptions and previous analytical results. the first layer included environmental and geographic dissimilarities; the second layer consisted of differences in community composition and diversity; and the third layer represented differences in niche breadth. separate sems were constructed for bacteria, fungi, and plants to identify taxon-specific pathways through which environmental changes influenced the niche breadth via community composition and diversity. nonsignificant paths were iteratively removed to optimize the model fit, and the direct, indirect, and total path effects stability and global change response niche breadth can be viewed as the functional occupation range of a community within environmental space, reflecting its overall capacity to utilize resources and respond to environmental variability . it is therefore not only an outcome of community structure but also a key indicator of ecosystem stability and adaptive potential. previous studies have shown that under strong biotic interactions, increases in species richness may lead to niche narrowing through enhanced niche differentiation . however, at the community level, we observed a significant positive relationship between diversity and niche breadth ( fig. 4d-f ), suggesting that in systems with high environmental heterogeneity or resource availability, increasing species diversity may expand the overall niche space through functional complementarity and resource partitioning . therefore, niche breadth is not governed solely by competition or environmental filtering but rather by the balance between these processes . in this context, biodiversity loss may not only reduce species richness but also alter internal niche structure. in systems dominated by biotic interactions, declining diversity may weaken competitive constraints and modify niche differentiation processes, whereas in environmentally driven systems, it may lead to contraction of niche space, thereby reducing ecosystem adaptive capacity under environmental change . in the context of global change, the mechanisms underlying niche breadth formation have important predictive implications . our results indicate that in alpine grassland ecosystems, abiotic factors influence niche breadth not only through direct pathways but also indirectly via biotic processes such as community diversity and composition. this dual regulation mechanism is consistently observed across different biological groups, suggesting a certain degree of generality. notably, these indirect pathways may be particularly susceptible to perturbation under global change. for example, as our results show that mean annual temperature and precipitation are key environmental drivers of niche breadth ( fig. 3a ), changes in temperature and precipitation regimes may influence species distributions and community assembly processes, thereby reshaping niche structure and community adaptive capacity . therefore, predicting ecosystem responses to environmental change requires integrating both the direct effects of abiotic drivers and the cascading effects mediated through changes in community diversity and composition. on this basis, from the perspective of ecosystem management and biodiversity conservation, niche breadth and its distribution in environmental space not only reflect how communities respond to environmental change but also indicate the potential capacity of ecosystems to maintain key functions . therefore, focusing solely on species richness may be insufficient to fully assess ecosystem stability; instead, it is necessary to consider the coordinated changes in community structure and niche characteristics under environmental change. maintaining high niche diversity and functional differentiation can enhance the buffering capacity of ecosystems against global change and improve their long-term stability and resilience. conclusion this study revealed distinct ecological strategies across biological groups in response to environmental gradients in world's highest plateau. fungal communities exhibited broader niche breadths than bacterial and plant communities, while plant communities displayed the highest variation in niche breadth across sites. bacterial and plant niche breadths were more strongly regulated by biotic factors. in contrast, the fungal niche breadth was primarily driven by environmental factors, both directly and indirectly. abiotic factors influence niche breadth directly and indirectly by shaping community diversity and composition. these findings emphasize the importance of biotic-abiotic interactions in determining community-level environmental adaptability, as well as specificity of fungal niche breadth pattern. we suggest niche breadth can serve as a valuable indicator for understanding how ecosystems respond to environmental changes. this cross-kingdom perspective deepens our understanding of the mechanisms underlying ecosystem stability and provides theoretical support for biodiversity conservation and management of alpine grasslands in the context of climate change. we also thank liang chen, renmin yang, and as rare event rates, small effective sample sizes, high-dimensional feature spaces, weak signals, population heterogeneity, and concerns over patient privacy. to overcome these obstacles and improve the precision of prognostic modeling, we introduce the survkl software, which enables the incorporation of external summary-level information with newly collected time-to-event data to support more robust and accurate predictions in survival analysis. our method adaptively adjusts the weight given to external information, down-weighting heterogeneous information and highlighting more informative ones. the proposed tool accommodates both low-dimensional and high-dimensional data, offering unpenalized estimation and computationally efficient lasso, ridge, and elastic net penalties. the survkl challenges like limited effective sample sizes, high dimensionality, low signal-to-noise ratios, and patient privacy concerns. although integrating external information is expected to enhance prediction performance, classical integration approaches often fail due to the unrealistic assumption of similar underlying distributions across data sources. thus, it is crucial to develop a transfer learning procedure that effectively accounts for population differences. although kullback-leibler (kl) divergence has been proposed to integrate external predicted probabilities for binary outcomes ( schapire et al . 2016 ), such approaches are not directly applicable to censored time-to-event data. in survival analysis, censored outcomes provide only partial information: they indicate that the event of interest has not occurred up to the observed censoring time but do not reveal the actual failure time. this incomplete observation complicates the direct computation of probability distributions over failure times, which is required for applying kl divergence. moreover, published risk scores for time-to-event data, such as polygenic hazard scores ( seibert et al . 2018 ), which are computed as weighted sums of single-nucleotide polymorphisms using effect sizes from cox models ( cox 1972 ), typically include only covariate coefficients without baseline hazard information. as a result, although these risk scores remain clinically valuable, their lack of a direct probabilistic interpretation prevents their use by existing integrated methods ( chen et al . 2023 ) that 2026 ) methods, require individual-level external data, which is often unavailable because of privacy constraints. to address these issues, we previously proposed a partial likelihood kl-based progress, ready-to-use software implementing transfer-learning methods for survival data remains scarce, which limits their adoption in practice. moreover, another common challenge arises from the use although useful for clinical decision making, such groupings are based solely on clinical knowledge, lack a probabilistic interpretation, and are not compatible with existing integration methods. to please see paragraphs 4.2 and 5 of our terms ( https://www.dovepress.com/terms.php ). abstract chronic pain represents a significant global public health burden, affecting millions of individuals and substantially impairing quality of life. however, its clinical management is largely limited by the modest efficacy and considerable adverse effects of current pharmacological interventions, highlighting an urgent need for safe and effective non-pharmacological alternatives. transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (tavns), a non-invasive neuromodulation technique, has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy. this narrative review provides a comprehensive, clinically oriented overview of tavns in chronic pain management, integrating mechanistic insights from preclinical and human studies, appraising the breadth and limitations of existing clinical evidence across pain phenotypes, and delineating key translational barriers. future directions are proposed to guide both research priorities and clinical decision-making. keywords transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation chronic pain neuromodulation non-pharmacological intervention analgesia funding this research received no external funding. it affects approximately 30% of the global population and constitutes a substantial public health challenge. 1 , 2 in recent years, chronic pain has been increasingly recognized as an independent clinical entity rather than merely a symptom. it is characterized by complex pathophysiological mechanisms, including nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic (central sensitization) components. it is also frequently comorbid with psychosocial disturbances, such as anxiety and depression. 3-5 beyond its detrimental effects on physical function, sleep quality, and overall quality of life, chronic pain imposes a considerable socioeconomic burden on healthcare systems and society. 6 in clinical practice for chronic pain, traditional pharmacological treatments have long occupied a dominant position; however, their limitations have become increasingly apparent. 7 long-term use of commonly used pharmacological agents is often associated with various adverse effects, including gastrointestinal injury, cardiovascular risks, addiction potential, and cognitive impairment. 8-10 these agents include nsaids, antiepileptic drugs, antidepressants, and opioids, each carrying distinct adverse effect profiles. meanwhile, interventional treatments such as nerve blocks and implantable neuromodulation demonstrate certain efficacy; however, they are constrained by invasive risks, high costs, and strict indications, which significantly limit their clinical applicability. 7 these therapeutic limitations frequently lead to suboptimal pain control, leaving a substantial unmet clinical need. this unmet need has catalyzed a paradigm shift toward personalized, multidisciplinary, and multimodal pain management. in this context, non-invasive neuromodulation has emerged as a prominent therapeutic strategy. 11-13 these modalities offer a compelling combination of robust safety and excellent patient tolerability, generating substantial interest across clinical and research domains. among these neuromodulatory approaches, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (tavns) exhibits encouraging preliminary therapeutic potential. it produces clinically meaningful analgesia across diverse chronic pain phenotypes, including musculoskeletal, neuropathic, visceral, and autoimmune-related pain, as well as chronic primary pain syndromes. the underlying mechanisms are multifactorial, including multi-target neurotransmitter modulation, activation of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (cap), autonomic nervous system rebalancing, and central network remodeling. neurologist james corning indirectly regulated vagal tone via carotid compression in the 1880s. 14 , 15 although this was not true vagus stimulation, corning's pioneering work laid the groundwork for neuromodulation. 16 before tavns, invasive implantable vns dominated but was limited by high costs, surgical trauma and procedural complications. 17 to overcome these drawbacks, non-invasive strategies were explored. in 2000, ventureyra proposed transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation as a non-invasive paradigm shift. 18 subsequent technical advances validated the auricular vagal branch as a feasible stimulation target. 19 , 20 tavns delivers electrical stimuli to superficial auricular vagal fibers, balancing promising efficacy and favourable safety. this innovation eliminates surgical risks, lowers medical expenses, and improves patient access and adherence. furthermore, it establishes a novel non-pharmacological modality for chronic pain treatment ( figure 1 ). a transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation device with ear electrode, cable and stimulator. since its introduction in 2000, tavns has gained increasing attention as a non-pharmacological option for chronic pain. accumulating evidence over the past two decades supports its analgesic efficacy across diverse conditions. nevertheless, existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses have largely focused on discrete pain types, such as migraine, fibromyalgia, or osteoarthritis. consequently, its broader applicability across the chronic pain spectrum remains insufficiently characterized. 21-23 although the literature has grown rapidly in recent years, findings remain fragmented across different conditions and study designs. therefore, the present narrative review integrates evidence across various chronic pain conditions to systematically examine the mechanisms of action and clinical utility of tavns. by synthesizing mechanistic, technical, and clinical evidence, this review aims to provide clinicians and researchers with a comprehensive framework for understanding tavns as a versatile non-pharmacological approach to pain management. furthermore, by highlighting gaps in current evidence, this review aims to inform future research and facilitate the clinical translation of tavns. methods this narrative review was conducted following the scale for the assessment of narrative review articles (sanra) guidelines to ensure methodological rigor and clinical relevance. to enhance methodological transparency, we provide below a detailed textual breakdown of the literature screening steps. although prisma reporting is not mandatory for narrative reviews, this review covers five distinct major chronic pain subtypes and synthesizes highly heterogeneous primary studies. without transparent screening metrics, readers cannot verify whether the literature selection process was systematic or detect potential selective citation bias. literature search strategy a systematic literature search was performed across pubmed/medline, embase, web of science, and the cochrane library from database inception to june 2026. all manuscripts published in 2026 and identified through the search were manually double-screened to capture the most up-to-date preclinical and clinical evidence. search terms combined medical subject headings (mesh) and free-text keywords related to three core domains: (i) transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation; (ii) chronic pain conditions; and (iii) neuromodulation-related outcomes. the detailed pubmed/medline search strategy is presented below. analogous search strings were adapted for the other databases according to their respective syntax and controlled vocabulary rules. exclusion criteria included case reports, conference abstracts, editorials, letters, and studies exclusively investigating invasive implantable vagus nerve stimulation. study selection and data extraction two authors independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disagreements resolved through discussion and consensus. stepwise literature screening volume description initial database searches retrieved 1916 records. after eliminating 648 duplicate publications, 1268 unique citations proceeded to title and abstract screening. a total of 1105 articles were excluded as irrelevant at this stage, leaving 163 papers for full-text assessment. after full-text review, 119 articles were excluded for failing to meet the inclusion criteria, yielding a final pool of 44 eligible primary studies on tavns and chronic pain. among these 44 studies, 28 are cited in the dedicated section "clinical evidence for tavns in chronic pain". the remaining 16 pain studies are not listed in this clinical subsection, as this review prioritizes thematic narrative integration rather than exhaustive individual study enumeration. the full reference list of this narrative review contains 104 citations in total, encompassing mechanistic animal experiments, neuroimaging trials, methodological reviews, and the 28 clinical/preclinical pain studies. the following data were extracted from each included study: first author, publication year, study design, sample size, pain phenotype, stimulation parameters (target site, frequency, pulse width, intensity, and duration), primary and secondary outcome measures, follow-up duration, and reported adverse events. evidence synthesis and quality assessment given the substantial heterogeneity across studies in terms of pain conditions, stimulation protocols, outcome instruments, and study designs, a formal meta-analysis was deemed inappropriate. instead, a narrative synthesis was employed, with evidence organized thematically by pain category into neurobiological mechanisms and clinical applications by pain category. consistent with the narrative review approach, formal risk-of-bias scoring was not performed. rather, evidence was interpreted with explicit consideration of study design features, sample size, control conditions, and follow-up duration. specifically, randomized sham-controlled trials were given greater weight in drawing clinical conclusions when such trials were available. tavns neurobiology: from peripheral stimulation to central modulation the vagus nerve (cranial nerve x) is one of the longest and most important mixed nerves in the human body; approximately 80% of its fibers are afferent. 24-26 it serves as a core bidirectional pathway connecting the central nervous system with visceral organs. through a complex neuroendocrine-immune network, it regulates physiological homeostasis and modulates inflammation, emotion, and nociception. the auricular branch of the vagus nerve (arnold's nerve) is the only cutaneous branch of this nerve. its nerve endings are highly concentrated in the auricular concha region, particularly the cymba conchae. 24 , 26 , 27 this relatively accessible surface anatomical localization renders the auricular concha region a practical target for tavns, although interindividual variability in nerve distribution remains a consideration. recent clinical and preclinical studies have unveiled the multifaceted analgesic mechanisms of tavns. these mechanisms operate through four principal pathways: neurotransmitter modulation, anti-inflammatory immunoregulation, autonomic functional reorganization, and central network neuroplasticity 28 ( figure 2 ). diagrams were created with biorender.com. diagram of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve modulate central pain pathway, highlighting brain regions like lc, rn and nts. 2) neurotransmitter modulation, showing increases in gaba, 5-ht, ne, ach and beta-endorphin, with a decrease in substance p. 3) cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, involving macrophages and cytokines like tnf-alpha, il-6 and il-1 beta. 4) autonomic rebalancing, indicating changes in parasympathetic and sympathetic activity, with tavns affecting heart rate variability. 5) bdnf-mediated neuroplasticity, focusing on synaptic plasticity in key brain regions. 6) large-scale network remodeling, involving sn and dmn networks. anatomical substrate: activation of the nts-pag descending pathway auricular vagal afferents project to the nucleus tractus solitarius (nts) in the brainstem; efferent projections from the nts connect to the pag, the core node of the endogenous analgesic neural circuit. 29 this auricle-jugular ganglion-nts-pag circuit provides the anatomical foundation for the neurotransmitter-mediated mechanisms detailed below. multi-target modulation of neurotransmitter systems tavns modulates nociceptive processing through the regulation of multiple neurotransmitter systems. the specific mechanisms encompass the following four aspects: enhancement of gabaergic inhibitory transmission as the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system, gaba suppresses neuronal hyperexcitability within nociceptive circuits, particularly at the level of key pain-modulatory nuclei. tavns enhances gabaergic transmission in these nuclei, including the periaqueductal gray and thalamic nuclei critically involved in nociceptive gating, thereby attenuating nociceptive signal transmission. 30 activation of the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine system the locus coeruleus constitutes the principal noradrenergic nucleus in the central nervous system, which sends ascending projections to the hypothalamus, amygdala, and prefrontal cortex as well as descending projections to the spinal cord dorsal horn. tavns activates this system, promoting norepinephrine release and thereby enhancing descending noradrenergic inhibition of ascending nociceptive transmission. 31 facilitation of descending serotonergic modulation tavns enhances the activity of serotonergic neurons in the nucleus raphe magnus and adjacent raphe obscurus/pallidus, thereby facilitating descending serotonergic inhibition of nociceptive transmission at the spinal dorsal horn. 26 while these neurotransmitter systems likely constitute the neurochemical substrate of tavns-mediated analgesia, their specific regulatory pathways, potential synergistic interactions, and clinical translation remain to be validated through rigorous randomized controlled trials. immunoregulation via the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (cap) is a vagus nerve-mediated neuro-immunomodulatory mechanism that prevents tissue damage and cell death by inhibiting excessive cytokine release. 35 , 36 this mechanism attenuates tissue damage caused by excessive cytokine release and alleviates inflammatory pain in various conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis (ra) and inflammatory bowel disease (ibd). tavns may engage this pathway indirectly through afferent-efferent vagal reflex arcs. 37 while systemic anti-inflammatory effects represent a plausible outcome, the underlying neural circuitry remains incompletely mapped, and direct evidence for such coupling in humans is currently lacking. reconstruction and balance of autonomic nervous function chronic pain is frequently accompanied by autonomic dysfunction, characterized by increased sympathetic activity and decreased parasympathetic tone. tavns enhances parasympathetic output and suppresses sympathetic hyperactivity through transcutaneous stimulation of vagal afferent fibers. 38 studies have shown that tavns significantly improves parasympathetic heart rate variability (hrv) indices, including rmssd and hf power, while reducing the lf/hf ratio, a marker of sympathovagal balance. microneurography recordings demonstrate that burst incidence of muscle sympathetic nerve activity is significantly reduced during tavns. 39 these acute findings suggest that tavns transiently restores autonomic balance, thereby alleviating pain-related autonomic dysregulation and associated stress responses. this sympathovagal rebalancing offers a mechanistic rationale for tavns application in sympathetically maintained pain conditions, such as complex regional pain syndrome. 40 bdnf is abundantly expressed in key supraspinal pain-modulatory regions, including the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, and periaqueductal gray (pag). 41 , 42 at the spinal level, bdnf is present in the superficial dorsal horn (laminae i-ii), where it modulates nociceptive transmission. 43 by enhancing bdnf-mediated synaptic plasticity across these supraspinal and spinal circuits, tavns may promote adaptive neural reorganization and contribute to analgesia. circuit level functional magnetic resonance imaging (fmri) evidence from multiple studies demonstrates that tavns differentially remodels the functional connectivity of thalamus-related brain circuits. specifically, it markedly strengthens the functional coupling between motor-associated thalamic subregions and the rostral anterior cingulate cortex/medial prefrontal cortex (racc/mpfc). this enhanced coupling facilitates the central descending pathways for anti-inflammation and endogenous analgesia. meanwhile, it weakens connectivity between occipital-linked thalamic subregions and the postcentral gyrus as well as the precuneus, thus alleviating central sensitization induced by overexcitation of the somatosensory cortex. these findings illustrate the neuroimaging mechanism at the central level underlying the dual anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects of tavns at the neural circuit level. 44-46 network level tavns modulates brain function at the macro network level by regulating the dynamic balance of large-scale intrinsic brain networks, mainly the default mode network (dmn) and salience network (sn). 47 the dmn controls resting-state spontaneous activity and self-referential cognition, while the sn mediates the detection of salient stimuli and transitions between brain states. aberrant activation and disrupted functional coordination between the two networks commonly lead to cognitive and neural dysfunction. as a non-invasive neuromodulation technique, tavns can normalize aberrant activation and functional connectivity within the dmn and sn, restore balanced inter-network dynamics, and thereby stabilize overall brain network function. in summary, tavns modulates multiple regulatory levels, thereby engaging a multi-dimensional pain modulation network. at the neurochemical level, it enhances gabaergic, noradrenergic, serotonergic, and endogenous opioid transmission to suppress nociceptive signaling. at the neuroplastic level, it upregulates bdnf-mediated synaptic plasticity across supraspinal and spinal circuits and remodels thalamocortical connectivity. at the network level, it regulates the dynamic balance between the dmn and sn. this multi-target, integrative mechanism underlies its distinct therapeutic advantages in chronic pain, particularly in conditions characterized standard stimulation pattern; 4 weeks may be too short. musculoskeletal disorders knee osteoarthritis knee osteoarthritis (koa) represents a prevalent age-related degenerative joint disorder characterized by persistent nociceptive and nociplastic pain, which imposes heavy individual and socioeconomic burdens worldwide. 72 as a novel non-invasive neuromodulation approach, tavns has garnered growing interest for its therapeutic potential in this condition. elsehrawy et al 48 reported a 12-week single-blind sham-controlled rct enrolling 68 bilateral koa patients, randomized to active tavns (n=34) and sham earlobe stimulation (n=34). the tavns group showed sustained, superior improvements in bilateral/remote elbow pressure pain threshold (ppt), nociceptive pain (vas), neuropathic pain markers (pd-q, dn4), central sensitization inventory (csi), physical function (koos, mobility tests), and mood (hads). sham stimulation only yielded transient vas relief that vanished at follow-up, with no lasting changes in sensitization, function and emotional indices. the intervention demonstrated favourable safety: only mild local tingling and skin irritation were reported, and no severe adverse events were recorded. evaluations were conducted at baseline, immediately post-stimulation, and 15 min after intervention. single-session tavns induced modest, short-lived knee pain reduction and elevated high-frequency heart rate variability (hf-hrv), reflecting transient parasympathetic enhancement alongside improved conditioned pain modulation (cpm). however, ppt and temporal summation (ts) remained unaltered post-intervention. notably, this open-label pilot lacked a sham comparator and only captured short-term outcomes without prolonged follow-up, limiting its causal interpretability relative to elsehrawy's controlled long-term trial. the two trials jointly suggest an exposure-dependent analgesic effect in koa, with distinct mechanistic patterns distinguishing acute from repeated stimulation. single-session tavns generates temporary pain relief via transient autonomic and descending inhibitory pathways, yet stable shifts in ppt and ts were absent in aoyagi's cohort. crucially, the absence of altered sensitization markers following a single tavns session does not inherently indicate an inability to reverse established central sensitization. isolated brief stimulation lacks sufficient exposure duration to induce persistent neural remodelling, representing an intrinsic limitation of single-session study designs rather than evidence of treatment inefficacy. by contrast, 12 weeks of repeated tavns in elsehrawy's rct produced durable elevations in multi-site ppt that persisted four weeks after treatment cessation, accompanied by sustained functional and psychological gains. this stark divergence implies that recurring tavns exposure may be required for long-term central neuroplasticity and stable desensitization. collectively, these data support a biphasic analgesic model: acute tavns delivers fleeting symptomatic relief mediated by autonomic signalling, while repeated regimens are required to reverse chronic central sensitization. future direct comparative sham-controlled trials contrasting single versus multi-week tavns paradigms are warranted to establish minimum effective doses. chronic low back pain chronic low back pain (clbp) ranks among the top global contributors to years lived with disability. population-level global burden of disease projections 73 , 74 estimate that around 39% of adults worldwide experience low back pain annually, with over 800 million cases anticipated by 2050 due to population aging. conventional management including pharmacology, physical modalities, and psychological care often yields suboptimal long-term relief for many patients. this shortfall creates an unmet clinical demand for non-invasive neuromodulation such as tavns. assessments were conducted at baseline, month 1, and month 3. progressive, statistically significant pain reduction was captured: vas fell by 16.1 mm at month 1 and 22.5 mm at month 3 (both p 0.001). composite improvements in physical disability, pain catastrophizing, life quality and mood-related distress were consistently observed across follow-up visits. moderate treatment adherence was documented, and only minor transient adverse events emerged without serious safety incidents. these findings confirm that tavns is well tolerated for long-term standalone use. for combined rehabilitation scenarios, gamze demircioglu et al 51 implemented a 3-week randomized trial that lacked a dedicated tavns sham group. they assigned 60 clbp patients to either tavns plus home exercise or standard physical modalities (hot pack, tens, ultrasound) plus identical exercise training. after three weeks of intervention, the tavns arm demonstrated superior outcomes in pain intensity, trunk muscle strength/endurance and sleep metrics. together, these mechanisms produce complementary analgesic benefits when tavns is paired with exercise. this supports tavns as a valuable adjunct for patients unresponsive to routine physical therapy. the two clbp trials differed substantially in intervention duration (3 weeks versus 3 months). notably, neither trial incorporated tavns sham stimulation as a control arm: tavares-figueiredo's single-arm design lacked any comparative reference, while demircioglu's control group only compared against conventional physical therapy, rather than inactive auricular stimulation. heterogeneous stimulation protocols, inconsistent treatment durations, and the lack of long-term post-intervention follow-up further preclude generalizable conclusions regarding the optimal tavns dosing regimen and sustained therapeutic effects. therefore, future standardized, sham-controlled randomized clinical trials with extended observation periods are needed to confirm effective treatment protocols and identify the clinical characteristics of responders to tavns for clbp treatment. temporomandibular disorders temporomandibular disorders (tmd) represent a complex
